verdict.identity: Murray River system; representative mainstem identity only (Western Australia)
verdict.status: Supported representative system/mainstem identity; uniform whole-group and per-reach naming are not cleared.
verdict.identity_confidence: High for representative regional system identity; exact headwater and estuarine transition boundaries unresolved.
verdict.scope: The selected historical baseline group only, with explicit tributary and estuarine exclusions from uniform naming.
verdict.korean_note: No direct Korean naming evidence acquired.

geometry_integrity.review_note: All decoded parts were included in the plot and numeric checks. Equal part/reach counts do not prove a reach-to-part correspondence.

spatial_identity_check.method: Complete baseline path plotted and all parts, counts, bounds and hashes checked, followed by side-by-side visual comparison with complete official regional maps and inspected course descriptions. No georegistered overlay or exact line fit.
spatial_identity_check.regional_course_comparison: The full inland route is consistent with the Hotham-to-Murray corridor shown in SLUI38, continuing through the Darling Range and Pinjarra area toward Peel Inlet. Its westward then northward terminal continuation extends beyond the named Murray river course.
spatial_identity_check.named_transition_check: The Hotham upstream association is a regional map inference; the source distinguishes the Hotham-Williams confluence from the downstream Murray. No source-to-rendered-part boundary or per-reach name assignment is established.
spatial_identity_check.bounded_unresolved_scope: Hotham-to-Murray, river-to-estuary and estuary-to-ocean transition boundaries are not established at source-reach resolution. Both fragments remain excluded from scalar naming clearance.
spatial_identity_check.western_murray_disambiguation: Western Australian Murray near Narrogin, Boddington, Pinjarra and Mandurah; this finding does not concern the Murray-Darling river in southeastern Australia.

outlet_scope.regional_location: Peel Inlet / Mandurah estuary-to-ocean corridor, Western Australia
outlet_scope.regional_receiving_water: Murray enters Peel-Harvey Estuary; the selected network continues toward the Indian Ocean
outlet_scope.endpoint_interpretation: The sea terminal describes the selected drainage continuation, not a claim that the named Murray River mouth lies at the ocean endpoint.

estuarine_continuation_review.stage2_interpretation: A short northward estuary-to-ocean connector, geographically consistent with the Mandurah Channel corridor; exact named-channel geometry is not independently verified.

remaining_limits: Only the pinned historical baseline was checked; current deployment and original HydroRIVERS coordinate equality are not claimed.
No exact name-boundary crosswalk or universal component name is established.
Representative identity does not authorize automatic changes.
